significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that, for a class of factual-QA errors, a correctly retrieved fact is causally defeated by late components that "track heuristic features (token frequency, recency, string similarity to the subject)," with the winner predictable from the "strength gap between the retrieved-fact direction and the heuristic direction." This combines a form-(ii) causal decomposition with a proposed form-(iii) predictive coupling: it would separate retrieval from answer selection and predict how changing either residual-stream contribution changes the answer, a distinction relevant to the component-level accounts of factual recall in Meng et al. (2022), "Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT," and Geva et al. (2023), "Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models." It establishes both a phenomenon—the knowing-versus-saying failure—and a mechanism, but "in some failures" and "a measurable fraction" leave the prevalence indeterminate; a negative result would rule out this small-component heuristic-override account, not dormant knowledge or retrieval-output dissociation generally. In the topic-substitution check, the broad question of why stored knowledge fails to influence answers would merit no above-median score by itself; the specific late override and strength-gap relation are what raise this modestly above the obvious topic-level hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handles named by the claim are the "dot-product gap between fact and heuristic directions" as a diagnostic or predictor and "ablating or down-weighting" override components as an intervention. The intervention can act ex ante, before token selection, although the gap is measured in the final residual stream and therefore supplies only very short lead time rather than screening a model or dataset well in advance. Because the hypothesis asserts only "a class of failures" and does not claim invariance across model families, re-extraction on another model would supply a procedure for finding new directions and components, not a quantitative relation that predicts that model's numbers; likely downstream users are factuality and interpretability researchers rather than general deployment practitioners. The topic-substitution check yields at most the median reach for generic knowledge-retrieval research; the concrete intervention and predictor survive deletion of the experimental details and support a reusable but per-model handle, so the score remains 6 rather than deriving from the topic's breadth.
